newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China raises price of domestic fuel oil - sources.
newsitem.headline: China raises price of domestic fuel oil - sources.

text.p: China, through its state-owned refiner SINOPEC, raised ex-refinery prices for fuel oil by 50 yuan to 900 yuan per tonne effective Oct 18, sources at SINOPEC said on Friday.
Separate officials said earlier on Friday that ex-refinery liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices were raised 400 yuan per tonne to 1,200 yuan.
SINOPEC has raised diesel prices by 90 yuan to 1,990 yuan. All price hikes were effective Oct 18.
Fuel oil is mainly used for power generation in China.
In U.S. dollar terms, that leaves ex-refinery prices of diesel at $240 per tonne, fuel oil at $108 per tonne and LPG at $145 per tonne.
Sources said SINOPEC adjusted product prices to support refining margins which were being eroded because of high crude oil feed prices and rising domestic demand.
